deck: Week 7, and I owe Arfan a correction. Last Tuesday I put a 3-3 team at No. 1, told you I ran the formula three times, and Arfan's review of that decision was one word, "crazyyy," with the extra y's doing a lot of work. Bazaan's was "These rankings r cap." Asim's defense of the desk was "The man ran it 3 times bazan," which I'd like on a shirt. Then Arfan scored 156.08, the second-best total anyone's posted this season, in a week where Bazaan and Mustafa both conceded their games on Thursday night, Bilal tried to reverse-Nazr two opponents and went one for two, the chat spent an hour making wide receiver puns at Asim, and Asim beat Haroon in the rematch while telling everyone his season was over. I ran it once this time. It said Arfan. Arfan's response to everyone else's response: "That juju don't work on me."

hnfnr-aint-busy.headline: THAT JUJU DON'T WORK ON ME
hnfnr-aint-busy.verdict: 156.08, the weekly high, the second check, 6-1, and the most points in the league. The one-week experiment at No. 2 is over. I regret nothing. (I regret it a little.)
hnfnr-aint-busy.analysis:
Burrow came back from the bye and threw for 28.88 against Baltimore. Tony Pollard scored 35.0 in a Titans loss, which I had to check twice because Tony Pollard scoring 35 points in 2026 sounds like something Bilal would type to curse him. Jaxon Smith-Njigba 26.8, Zay Flowers 23.7, Rhamondre Stevenson 20.0 from the flex on Thursday night. The only miss was Dominic Zvada, the kicker Arfan picked up for Dicker's bye, who scored 1.0, and Derrick Henry's 5.4 in a game the Ravens lost by 22 with Huntley at quarterback. 156.08. Bazaan looked at Stevenson's Thursday line and posted "Welp ggs I lost" at 8:48 PM with thirteen games left to play. He was right.

Here's what the chat did with Arfan's week, in order. Sunday afternoon, Asim: "Can you please relaxxxxxxx @Arfan. Give someone else a chanceeeeee." Then Bilal, trying the Nazr on purpose: "nawww you got it bro." Arfan: "@Bilal it ain't even like that." Tuesday, Bilal again: "I see you arfan 👀 #1 in pts scored shiiii." Asim: "Arfan ripping thru everyone every week he needs to be stopped." And then the line of the week, from the man himself: "That juju don't work on me." Yaseen, within a minute: "Would be a shame if something happened to JSN." Mustafa: "He says that with no hate in his heart." Arfan, wounded: "Why can't [anyone] be happy for you for a second." Nobody in this league has ever been happy for anyone for a second. That's the whole product.

The formula, which last week preferred Haroon by 2.3, prefers Arfan by 13 this week, and I'm not going to argue with it twice. 6-1, 55-22 against the field, 847.54 points, which passed Haroon for the league lead, and the Luckbox Index has him at a modest +1.00, which in this league is practically earned. Second weekly high of the season puts him at $200 collected, tied with Haroon, both still $167 in the hole, because the buy-in is $367 and I will keep saying it. Seven moves all year. Asim put it best on Tuesday: "What yall thought Haroon was going to be doing is exactly what Arfan is doing." Sunday he's at RN, where Mustafa has already told us, "I'm a luckbox." We'll see whose juju is whose.

team-noor.headline: ONE WEEK AT THE TOP
team-noor.verdict: 86.22, a loss to Asim in the Allen-for-Purdy rematch with Allen on bye, and 3-4. Tre Tucker scored 18.8 on the bench. You already know what Level that is.
team-noor.analysis:
The 3-3 favorite lasted exactly one week, which is about what the chat gave it. Haroon went into the rematch against Asim with Josh Allen and Keon Coleman on bye, Jared Goff at quarterback, and a Thursday forecast of his own: "It'll even out mostly likely. Watson and Hall might not play." Goff was fine (18.02). Kyren 17.1, Chase 14.7, Kittle 10.8. The problem was the back half of the lineup: Christian Watson 8.2, Dobbins 8.3, the Patriots defense at −1.0, and Aaron Jones at 3.1 in the flex after aggravating an MCL sprain in the fourth quarter. Tre Tucker, the hero of two weeks ago, scored 18.8 on the bench. Tucker over Jones wins the game by 3.7. That's a Dobbins Level loss, the second one for Haroon this season, and at this point the award should probably be renamed for him entirely.

The chat was unusually gracious about it, which tells you how much everybody likes Haroon and how much everybody was scared of Asim's mouth if he lost. Asim, Sunday night: "GGs harooooon. Did not expect that outcome." Haroon: "Good match." That's the whole exchange. Two weeks ago these two were trading evil-eye emojis over a quarterback. (Asim did get in "Idk what Haroon did to me after posting the eyes" on Thursday, when Puka's calf scared him, but Puka played and scored 17.8, so the eyes are officially 1-1.) The ledger on the trade now reads DEDDYBABA +63.84, with Allen's bye week counted as a zero, which is how bye weeks work and also how Haroon's season has gone.

The board moves him to second, and I want to be clear that second at 3-4 is still the formula talking: 823.0 points, 49-28 against the field, a Luckbox Index of −1.45. Only Naafay has been unluckier. He's fifth in the actual standings, a game out of the top four, with Chief sheikh up next and Kittle on bye. Asim's Tuesday summary, which I'll repeat because it's correct: "What yall thought Haroon was going to be doing is exactly what Arfan is doing." The thing is, the formula thinks Haroon is still doing it. The schedule just keeps disagreeing.

chief-sheikh.headline: THE SHEIKH BOWL
chief-sheikh.verdict: 127.36 to 84.62 over the commissioner, with Kyler, Jefferson and St. Brown all back. McBride 22.1. Third on the board, third in the standings, third in all-play. Consistent.
chief-sheikh.analysis:
Kashir had every star back from the bye and used them like a man who'd been waiting two weeks to do it. Trey McBride 22.1, St. Brown 19.7, Love 16.96, Corum 16.6, Braelon Allen 16.4 in the flex, Warren 15.2, Aubrey 14.0. Jefferson was the only quiet one at 6.4. The Texans defense scored 0.0, which is an improvement on last week's −2.0 by exactly two points, and Omar Cooper Jr., a new name on the bench, scored 20.0 while Cam Skattebo scored 18.6 next to him. He won by 42.74. The Sheikh bowl was over by the early window, and Kashir, who narrates everything, posted nothing about it, which is the most respectful thing a Sheikh has ever done to another Sheikh.

What he did post was the opening line of the week's best bit. Thursday, 5:58 PM, after Asim's Puka panic: "Asim u need a wr asap step into my office." What followed was six managers making receiver puns at a man in crisis. Yaseen: "If you need a WR you know where to Diggs." Haroon: "You can Waddle over to my side." Mustafa: "Do you just need one receiver or do you need Moore." Kashir, closing his own thread: "Your team gonna be re Bourne." Yaseen: "Send me an offer if it's not too much of a Burden," followed two hours later by "Don't Burden yourself with sending me a trade for Luther. That boy not going anywhere." (Burden then scored 21.7. Of course he did.) Asim's contribution was two GIFs and "Lmfaooooo I'm dead." No trade happened. Nobody expected one to. Kashir also delivered Tuesday's wisdom: "Yall worried about championships when you should be worried about playoffs," which is the correct read in a league where seven teams are 3-4.

The board holds him at third, and he's third everywhere you look: standings at 4-3, all-play at 48-29, 769.02 points. Twenty moves on the season, and Kyler Murray, who was on this bench last week, is starting for Bazaan now, which I'll get to. The ceiling slips one spot to fourth because Bilal's full roster finally showed up, not because anything on Kashir's changed. Sunday it's at Team Noor with Skattebo and the Texans defense on bye. Haroon's unlucky, Kashir's third in everything, and somebody's going to be 4-4 and furious.

deddybaba.headline: RIP MY SEASON (5-2)
deddybaba.verdict: 98.22 in the rematch, four straight wins, second in the standings, and the luckiest team in the history of this league's spreadsheet. Asim declared the season over on Thursday. He won Sunday.
deddybaba.analysis:
Thursday, 5:24 PM, Bazaan: "Dang puka." Puka Nacua had left practice with a calf injury. Thursday, 5:30 PM, Asim: "Rip my season, was fun to get to second place while it lasted 🤣😭." Then "Idk what Haroon did to me after posting the eyes 🧿." Then "If I go down I'm taking everyone down with me," followed by "lol jk," which is the most Asim sequence of messages in the entire chat log. The MRI came back minor, Puka played and caught 17.8, and Asim beat Haroon in the rematch 98.22 to 86.22 behind Bucky Irving's 23.5, Ollie Gordon's 16.8, Kraft's 12.8 and Fairbairn's 11.0. He started Christian Kirk, who scored 0.0, and still won by twelve. He is 5-2, second in the standings, and on a four-game winning streak, and he opened Tuesday with "Mannn no one trading anymore or what."

The receiver situation that caused all this is real. With Tuten on bye he had Roschon Johnson in the flex for 1.3, Kirk at 0.0 and Rashee Rice questionable on the bench. Kashir offered his office. The rest of the league offered puns. Nabil offered perspective: "Chill asim you still got it. Puka is overrated." (Nabil traded CeeDee Lamb for a running back five weeks ago and is now the league's authority on which receivers are overrated.) Asim's Tuesday philosophy, which doubles as a confession: "Literally anyone can win the finals, record don't matter just getting a playoff spot matters." Arfan's reply: "Bro you #2. Why you trippin. Like relaxxxx."

Now the Luckbox Index, because it has to be said. Asim is 31-46 against the field, tenth, and the Index has him at +2.18, which is the largest number it has ever produced. The formula ranks him seventh. The desk ranks him fourth, and that's the desk's call, for the same reason as last week: he's 5-2, he's won four straight, and he beat Arfan and Haroon back to back. A model that has a 5-2 team seventh needs to see a standings page. The trade ledger is +63.84 over Haroon, Bucky's 23.5 leading the way, and the ceiling rises to sixth. Sunday is Bizzy at DEDDYBABA with Purdy and Kirk on bye, and Asim's already decided: "This is def going in Rameel's weekly video." Correct.

team-mbk.headline: THANOS
team-mbk.verdict: 132.0, the second-best score of the week, with Jacobs back, Judkins at 22.9 and Higgins at 23.8. Bilal reverse-Nazr'd Yaseen on Thursday and Yaseen scored 76. Then he tried it on Arfan.
team-mbk.analysis:
Tuesday night, reacting to last week's package: "I feel like I'm thanos tho! Every team I face turns into the effing avengers!" Five days later Bilal put up 132.0 against Yaseen, the first week all season his roster had everybody. Josh Jacobs came back and ran for 17.6. Quinshon Judkins, the guy Kashir said Bilal gave up two bench players for, scored 22.9 in the flex. Tee Higgins 23.8, London 16.1, Gibbs 14.8, Stafford 17.5. KC Concepcion scored 19.2 on the bench and Rico Dowdle 11.6, and Dak Prescott scored 23.28 behind Stafford, which means the Stafford Rule is back in its original form: the quarterback Bilal doesn't start outscores the one he does. The difference this week is that it didn't matter by 55 points.

The Nazr experiment. Thursday night, with Luther Burden torching the Patriots for Yaseen, Bilal posted "Your luck will run out soon Yaseen! 👀 sooner or later your bum team will fall!" and then, catching himself, "Sorry I meant your team is so great 👀👀👀👀👀👀." Yaseen scored 76.42. It worked. Emboldened, Bilal tried it on Arfan Sunday afternoon ("nawww you got it bro") and Tuesday ("I see you arfan 👀 #1 in pts scored"). Arfan scored 156.08 and announced the juju doesn't work on him. So the reverse Nazr is now 1-1, the forward Nazr only works on receivers, and the whole system needs a peer review. Bilal's other contribution was reviving Bilal's Law for Mustafa's benefit: "Fax no paper! @Mustafa bringing it back for you bro." Mustafa: "It was no printer fool."

The board moves him up two to fifth and the ceiling up to third, because this is the first week the roster the model has been pricing since August actually took the field. 3-4, sixth in the standings, 46-31 against the field, 781.72 points, and still a Luckbox Index of −1.18. He's scored more than Asim and Yaseen and is two games behind both. The trade with Ivan is down to +4.30 in Ivan's favor after Judkins' 22.9 against Evans and Montgomery's zeros, so the Kashir verdict of "two bench players for a starter" might get overturned by November. Sunday it's RamBam at Team MBK. The commissioner's team faces Bilal twice this year. This is the first one.

bizzy.headline: LET MY BOY DRAKE EAT
bizzy.verdict: 99.64 over RN, Maye 27.44, Lamb 21.9, Loveland started this time (16.4). 3-4, sixth on the board, and the Shough-over-Maye question is officially closed.
bizzy.analysis:
Last week Nabil benched Colston Loveland's 15.5 and lost by 1.9. This week he started Loveland, Loveland scored 16.4, and Nabil beat Mustafa by 23. That's the whole lesson of fantasy football and it took him exactly one week to learn it, which puts him ahead of most of this league. Drake Maye threw for 27.44 on Thursday night against Chicago, prompting Nabil's "Let my boy drake eat haha" and Mustafa's "Bro ain't no way pats score like that," which is a strange thing for Mustafa to say given he was the one losing to them. Lamb 21.9, McLaughlin 12.0. The misses were real too: Walker 7.7 against Seattle, Chase Brown 7.8, Nico Collins 1.6 in a Texans loss, DeMario Douglas 3.8 in the flex, the Rams defense 1.0. Tyler Shough scored 13.82 on the bench and Maye doubled him. Case closed.

Nabil's week in the chat was short and mostly advisory. He told Asim to chill and called Puka overrated, which from the man who traded CeeDee Lamb for Jonathan Taylor is a bold stance on receiver valuation. The ledger on that trade now reads RamBam +44.40, though this week's accounting was closer than the headline: Lamb and Chase Brown gave Nabil 29.7 in the lineup, Taylor and Emanuel Wilson gave the commissioner 36.0. Lamb is back to being Lamb. The trade is still a trade.

3-4, seventh in the standings, 38-39 against the field, 745.68 points, sixth on the board, up two. The structure's real: Maye is a top-five quarterback this year, Lamb is healthy, Loveland is starting. The question is whether Walker and Brown are a backfield or a rotation. Sunday he's at DEDDYBABA with Collins on bye, which given Collins' 1.6 is less of a loss than it sounds. Asim's 5-2. Nabil's concession timing is a tracked stat on this site. If this one gets to Monday night, I know who to watch.

rambam.headline: THE SHEIKH BOWL, FROM THE OTHER SIDELINE
rambam.verdict: 84.62 in the Sheikh bowl, down 42.74 to Kashir, with Daniels on bye. Three straight wins became one straight loss. 3-4, and the formula's not impressed.
rambam.analysis:
The plan was Stroud for Daniels' bye, and Stroud did his part: 16.52 in a Texans loss to the Giants. Jonathan Taylor and Emanuel Wilson scored 18.0 each, which is nice symmetry and also 36 points from the two backs the commissioner got in the Lamb trade. Everything after that went sideways. Matthew Golden 6.9. Xavier Worthy 2.6 in a Chiefs game where Kansas City scored three points total. Ryan Flournoy, a new name in the flex, 9.0. The Titans defense, picked up for the week, 0.0. Shrader 3.0. Hunter Henry 10.6 was the third-best starter, and Kaelon Black's 10.4 on the bench would have been fourth. 84.62 is the fourth-lowest score of the week and it lost to Kashir's 127.36 by the width of the entire Sheikh family tree.

The chat was quiet about it, which is its own kind of loud. Kashir didn't post a word about the result; he spent his week telling Asim to step into his office. No commissioner post, no "can your guy stop," no Monday night drama, because there wasn't any Monday night. The three-game winning streak that got RamBam to fourth on the board is over, and the formula, which does not grade on a curve for byes, drops him to sixth and the desk to seventh behind Nabil, who has more points and the same record.

3-4, eighth in the actual standings on the tiebreak, 38-39 against the field, 728.74 points, a Luckbox Index of −0.45. Nineteen moves, fourth-most in the league. The ledger on the Lamb trade is +44.40 and holding. Daniels is back Sunday against Bilal, who just scored 132 with his full roster for the first time, and the ceiling rank slides from fourth to fifth, not because anything broke, but because Bilal's roster finally arrived and the matrix only has twelve rows. The commissioner plays Team MBK twice this season. The first one is a bad week to be the commissioner.

gang-green.headline: I HAVE FULL HATE NOW
gang-green.verdict: 76.42, a second straight loss, 4-3, and Bryce Young at 5.42 in a 43-13 Panthers loss. Yaseen tried having no hate in his heart. He's updated his position.
gang-green.analysis:
Thursday night Yaseen was at the top of his game. Luther Burden scored 21.7 against New England in the flex, Bilal posted "Of course this [guy] would have a good game against me," and Yaseen replied "Cleanse ur heart brother," then spent the evening turning down trade offers for Burden with puns ("Don't Burden yourself with sending me a trade for Luther. That boy not going anywhere"). Then Sunday happened. Bryce Young, the return in the Adonai Mitchell trade, scored 5.42 as Tampa beat Carolina 43-13, and took Hubbard (8.0) and McMillan (6.0) down with him. Garrett Wilson 3.6. The Jets defense 0.0. Jason Sanders 4.0. Jeanty's 17.6 and Fannin's 10.1 were the only other starters in double digits, Trevor Lawrence was on bye, and Bilal scored 132 on the other side. The 4-2 team that was tied for second a week ago is 4-3 and fourth.

Tuesday's Yaseen, after a week of preaching: "Nah my team is ass." "I have full hate now." Bilal: "Lmfao embrace it Yaseen!!!" So the no-hate-in-your-heart theory of fantasy success, which went 4-1 in its first five weeks, has been formally abandoned by its author after two losses. In its place he's trying the Nazr, aimed at the top: "Would be a shame if something happened to JSN," to which Mustafa noted, "He says that with no hate in his heart." The Bazaan Transaction Rate has a Tokyo franchise now too: fifteen moves, with MarShawn Lloyd finally dropped after his 1.0 in the flex cost the RN game, and Dameon Pierce, Justice Hill and Jonathon Brooks all added.

The board. 4-3 and fourth in the standings, but 30-47 against the field, eleventh, with 678.66 points, tenth, and a Luckbox Index of +1.27. The formula ranks him ninth, behind a 2-5 team. The desk puts him eighth, because 4-3 is 4-3, and no higher, because the last two weeks were 79 and 76. The ceiling stays at eight. The ledger on the Young trade reads +60.36, and it's starting to feel like the kind of lead you'd rather not have. Sunday is at I Eat Ass, who's won two straight. Yaseen has full hate now. Let's see what it's worth.

i-eat-ass.headline: THE SILENT TREATMENT
i-eat-ass.verdict: 114.9 over Naafay, Jameson Williams 23.6 from the flex, two straight wins, 3-4. Ivan didn't post a word all week. The desk moves him up three. Don't tell him.
i-eat-ass.analysis:
Ivan is the only manager in this league who went an entire week without typing anything, and he's the only one who went 1-0 against a team that outscored the league average. That's not a coincidence. That's a man who's learned something. Jameson Williams, who was on the bench two weeks ago with the Lions on bye, scored 23.6 in the flex against Green Bay. Cousins 20.4, McCaffrey 19.0 on a questionable tag, Boswell 11.0 in his first week replacing Zvada (who went to Arfan and scored 1.0, so that worked out for exactly one of them). Olave and Woody Marks 8.6 each, Tate 7.4, Goedert 7.3, the Steelers 9.0. Nothing spectacular, nothing under seven, and a 6.78-point win over Naafay. Vele's 13.9 and Hockenson's 11.5 on the bench were insurance he didn't need.

The bad news column is the same as last week, which is at least stable. Jalen Hurts is off the roster entirely now, which the desk will note and leave alone. Mike Evans was out with the ribs and the Achilles; David Montgomery was out too. The Judkins trade, which Ivan was winning by 27.20 last Tuesday, is down to +4.30 after Judkins scored 22.9 for Bilal and both of Ivan's guys scored zero. Bilal gets to say "I told you so" by the end of next week if Evans doesn't play. Kashir's "Can't believe we let Ivan fleece you" is one more week from being filed under Corrections.

The board moves him up three, to ninth, and that's the desk's call rather than the formula's, which had him tenth: 3-4, two straight wins, 34-43 against the field, 717.64 points, and a Luckbox Index of −0.09, which is the closest anyone in this league is to deserving exactly what they've gotten. The ceiling stays at twelve, because the roster that drafted Hurts is now the roster with Cousins, and because McCaffrey, Olave and Vele are all on bye Sunday against Yaseen, who has full hate now. Ivan's going to need a flex. He'll find one. He didn't say anything, and that's been working.

bazan.headline: WELP GGS I LOST
bazan.verdict: 61.4, the week's low, with Kyler Murray starting, the Panthers defense at −3.0 and a kicker at 1.0. Bazaan conceded at 8:48 PM Thursday. Seven moves later, he was right.
bazan.analysis:
Let me set the scene. Thursday night, Patriots at Bears, 8:48 PM. Bazaan has one player in the game (A.J. Brown, who'll finish with 6.3) and Arfan has Rhamondre Stevenson, who's on his way to 20.0. Thirteen of the fourteen games on the schedule haven't kicked off. Bazaan: "Welp ggs I lost." Twenty minutes later Mustafa, also losing a Thursday night game, posts "Same." Two men conceding fantasy matchups with 92 percent of the week remaining is a new Kingwood record for giving up, and the thing is, both were correct. Bazaan finished at 61.4, the week's low. Kyler Murray, who was on Kashir's bench last Tuesday and Bazaan's roster by the weekend, started and scored 13.9. Swift 17.0, Nabers 14.6. Then it fell off a cliff: Bam Knight 7.8, A.J. Brown 6.3, Higbee 2.4, Jalen Coker 1.4, Ryan Fitzgerald 1.0, and the Panthers defense −3.0 in a 43-13 loss. Aaron Rodgers scored 13.08 on the bench, and Lamar Jackson didn't play for the third straight week.

The transaction log, because it's the best recurring feature on this site: seven more moves this week, 37 on the season, eleven clear of anyone else. Folk out, Fitzgerald in. Huntley out, Kyler in. Ravens defense out, Panthers in. Juwan Johnson out, Higbee in (via Nabil's waiver pile). Dameon Pierce, who scored 13.0 for Bazaan two weeks ago, is now scoring 11.3 on Yaseen's bench. Over the last three weeks the defense and kicker slots have produced a −2.0, a 1.0, a −3.0 and another 1.0. At some point you have to ask whether the streaming is the problem, and I'm asking. His review of the site this week: "These rankings r cap," followed by "He needs to run it until it mentions me getting Ajb back." A.J. Brown is back. He scored 6.3. I ran it.

3-4, tenth in the standings, 33-44 against the field, 680.18 points, and a Luckbox Index that's still 0.00, which means Bazaan is still the only person in the league getting exactly what he deserves, and this week that was 61 points. The formula says eleventh. The desk says tenth, over Naafay, on record. The ceiling slides to ten because Lamar's third miss turns "targeting Week 7" into "no date," and James Cook was on bye on top of it. Sunday he's at IVaafay with Nabers on bye. Naafay is the unluckiest man in the league and Bazaan is the only one with zero luck. If Bazaan concedes early again, at least this time the math will be close.

ivaafay.headline: UNLUCKIEST MAN IN KINGWOOD
ivaafay.verdict: 108.12 and a loss to Ivan by 6.78. Three straight losses, 2-5, last place, and the fifth-best all-play record in the league. The Index says −1.64. Naafay says nothing.
ivaafay.analysis:
There's a version of this season where Naafay is 5-2. I know because the Real Standings page computes it: IVaafay is 40-37 against the entire field this year, fifth in the league, ahead of Bizzy, RamBam, Ivan, Bazaan, Asim and Yaseen. His actual record is 2-5. The Luckbox Index puts him at −1.64, the unluckiest anyone has been through seven weeks, and this week was the perfect specimen. 108.12 beats seven of the eleven other teams. Caleb Williams 22.12, Javonte 21.5, Bijan 14.7, Pickens 13.7, Pitts 10.7, Jordan Mason 6.8 in his first week back from IR. He lost to Ivan's 114.9 by less than a Jordan Mason (6.8). Two weeks ago it was Arfan. Last week it was Haroon's Tucker. This week it was Jameson Williams. Naafay didn't post a single message all week, which for a man who said "I can never beat Haroon" a week earlier is its own kind of statement.

A few notes on the roster, because he's been busy even if he's been silent. The Bears defense, dropped two weeks ago after a −2.0, is back after the Jaguars also scored −2.0; they scored 3.0, which is at least a positive number. Jake Bates, dropped for Butker, is also back. Deshaun Watson is gone; Caleb's the starter and he's been good for 16.5 and 22.12 in two weeks. Davante Adams is on IR for six to ten weeks. Jaylin Noel is a new name on the bench. Seventeen moves. The Bijan Build still has Bijan, who's scored 6.3 and 14.7 in the last two weeks, and that's the gap between the roster Naafay drafted and the one he's playing.

The board drops him one to eleventh, and this one's the desk, not the formula. The formula had him eighth, because the formula counts all-play and points, and his are fine. The desk counts 2-5 and a three-game losing streak, and puts him below Yaseen, Ivan and Bazaan, all 3-4 or better. That's the record-weighting Rameel asked for and it costs Naafay three spots this week. The ceiling moves up one to nine, which is the matrix's way of saying what the Index says: this roster is better than its record, and if the schedule ever turns, it's a problem. Sunday is Bazan at IVaafay. The unluckiest team in the league hosts the only one with zero luck. Somebody has to win it.

mustafas-magnificent-team.headline: SAME
mustafas-magnificent-team.verdict: 76.4, Mahomes at 6.0 in a 20-3 Chiefs loss, Likely 2.2, and a Thursday night concession. 3-4, two straight wins became one loss, and the all-play record is 20-57.
mustafas-magnificent-team.analysis:
Thursday morning, Mustafa posted "I'm a luckbox" unprompted, which is either a confession or a preemptive strike, and Thursday night at 9:08 PM, twenty minutes after Bazaan's "Welp ggs I lost," he posted "Same." Both were right. Patrick Mahomes scored 6.0 as the Chiefs lost 20-3 in Seattle, which is the kind of sentence that didn't exist three years ago. Isaiah Likely, the best tight end in Kingwood for two straight weeks, scored 2.2. Kelce 6.4. Germie Bernard, the waiver hit, 4.2. Kendre Miller 4.3. On the plus side, Saquon Barkley came back and scored 14.1, Makai Lemon, a new Eagles receiver on the roster, scored 16.2, the Vikings defense 11.0 and Reichard 12.0, and the lineup still lost by 23 to Nabil. J.J. McCarthy, the Giants quarterback, showed up on the bench with 10.18. Twenty-six moves. The lineup card changes every week and the number at the bottom keeps landing in the seventies.

The chat kept him busy anyway. The pun run got "Do you just need one receiver or do you need Moore" and "How's it going Ladd?" (Ladd McConkey, his own receiver, left with a concussion, so that one aged fast). When Bilal brought back Bilal's Law for his benefit ("Fax no paper! bringing it back for you bro"), Mustafa replied "It was no printer fool," which Asim rated above the original. And when Yaseen wished harm on JSN, Mustafa provided the week's best deadpan: "He says that with no hate in his heart." He's the league's best color commentator on weeks he loses, which is most of them.
